Edit: I have had a really quick scan through an unofficial paper that is supposedly similar to the actual paper, and most of my comment above stands - I really don't think this should be news worthy at all. The A-Level AQA physics paper from last year was far far worse comparatively, and I didn't see that make the news even once.

 I thought almost all the questions were very standard straight out of what you might see in a textbook, but there was a lot to get done within the time limit; exam pressure and nerves would definitely add to this, which is why I can understand how so many struggled. To add, this is also a step up in length and difficulty from recent past years, which most students will have used as their main tool for practice.

There were two questions on that paper, which people definitely will have struggled with, which required some lateral thinking. 

i) For the last question, you want to show a number of the form 2(2k+1) can't be square. This is tricky if you haven't seen it, but it's simply that 2 isn't a factor of the odd number 2k+1, so 2(2k+1) contains exactly one (which is odd) '2' in its prime factorisation, so it is not square.

ii) For finding a range for k such that k/x = |px-q| has exactly 3 solutions in x, drawing a sketch and noting that the left side of the modulus graph needed to intersect k/x would lead to solving a quadratic discriminant being > 0. Without the sketch, this is very hard to deduce for most students.
